source.text: כֹּ֤ה הִרְאַ֨נִי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִנֵּה֙ יוֹצֵ֣ר גֹּבַ֔י בִּתְחִלַּ֖ת עֲל֣וֹת הַלָּ֑קֶשׁ וְהִ֨נֵּה־לֶ֔קֶשׁ אַחַ֖ר גִּזֵּ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus showed me [the] Lord Yahweh, and look, he [was] forming locusts at [the] beginning of the coming up of the late crop; and look, [it was the] late crop after the mowings of the king.

en.L: Thus the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was forming locusts at the beginning of the coming up of the late crop; and look, [it was] the late crop after the king's mowings.
en.B: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was forming swarms of locusts just as the late crop was beginning to come up, the crop that grows after the king's share has been mown.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me a vision. He was making swarms of locusts. It was just when the second crop was starting to come up, after the king's share of the first crop had been cut.

es.L: Así me mostró el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: he aquí, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} formaba langostas al comienzo de la subida de la cosecha tardía; y he aquí, [era] la cosecha tardía después de las siegas del rey.
es.B: Esto es lo que me mostró el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba formando enjambres de langostas justo cuando comenzaba a brotar la cosecha tardía, la que crece después de que se ha segado la parte del rey.
es.R: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} me mostró una visión. Él estaba haciendo enjambres de langostas. Era justo cuando la segunda cosecha empezaba a brotar, después de que se había cortado la parte del rey de la primera cosecha.

fr.L: Ainsi me fit voir le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : voici, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} formait des sauterelles au début de la montée du regain ; et voici, [c’était] le regain après les fauchaisons du roi.
fr.B: Voici ce que le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} me fit voir : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} formait des nuées de sauterelles au moment où le regain commençait à pousser, le regain qui vient après qu’on a fauché la part du roi.
fr.R: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} m’a montré une vision. Il faisait des nuées de sauterelles. C’était juste au moment où la deuxième récolte commençait à pousser, après qu’on avait coupé la part du roi sur la première récolte.

sw.L: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alinionyesha hivi: tazama, alikuwa akiumba nzige mwanzoni mwa kuchipua kwa mmea wa pili; na tazama, [ulikuwa] mmea wa pili baada ya kukatwa kwa nyasi za mfalme.
sw.B: Hiki ndicho Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alichonionyesha: alikuwa akiumba makundi ya nzige wakati mmea wa pili ulipokuwa ukianza kuchipua, mmea unaoota baada ya fungu la mfalme kukatwa.
sw.R: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alinionyesha maono. Alikuwa akifanya makundi ya nzige. Ilikuwa wakati mazao ya pili yalipokuwa yakianza kuota, baada ya fungu la mfalme la mazao ya kwanza kukatwa.

vi.L: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy thế này: kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang tạo nên châu chấu vào lúc vụ mùa muộn bắt đầu mọc lên; và kìa, [ấy là] vụ mùa muộn sau những đợt cắt cỏ của vua.
vi.B: Đây là điều Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang tạo nên những đàn châu chấu đúng lúc vụ mùa muộn bắt đầu mọc lên, là vụ mùa mọc sau khi phần của vua đã được cắt.
vi.R: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy một khải tượng. Ngài đang làm ra những đàn châu chấu. Lúc ấy vụ mùa thứ hai vừa bắt đầu mọc lên, sau khi phần của vua trong vụ đầu đã được cắt.

ko.L: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 이와 같이 보여 주셨다. 보라, 늦은 풀이 돋아나기 시작할 때에 그분이 메뚜기들을 만들고 계셨다. 보라, [그것은] 왕이 풀을 벤 뒤에 [자라는] 늦은 풀이었다.
ko.B: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 보여 주신 것은 이러하다. 늦은 풀이 막 돋아나기 시작할 때에 그분은 메뚜기 떼를 만들고 계셨다. 그것은 왕의 몫을 벤 뒤에 자라는 풀이었다.
ko.R: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 환상을 보여 주셨다. 그분은 메뚜기 떼를 만들고 계셨다. 그때는 왕이 첫 번째 풀 가운데 자기 몫을 베어 간 뒤, 두 번째 풀이 막 돋아나기 시작할 때였다.

decisions.choice: the first of five visions
decisions.reason: Chapters 7-9 report five visions: the locusts (7:1-3), the fire (7:4-6), the plumb line (7:7-9), the basket of summer fruit (8:1-3) and the Lord beside the altar (9:1-4). The first four begin the same way, 'Thus the Lord GOD showed me'. In the first two Amos prays and the LORD relents; in the next two the LORD says that he will no longer pass by his people; in the last there is no dialogue at all. Amos tells the visions in prose, with his words and the LORD's as a conversation.

decisions.choice: the late crop after the king's mowings: the second growth of spring, after the king's share was cut
decisions.reason: Leqesh is the late growth that comes up with the spring rains. 'The king's mowings' seem to be a first cutting taken as tax, perhaps for the royal horses and herds (compare 1 Kings 18:5). The late crop was what the farmers had left for themselves and their animals; if locusts ate it, there would be nothing until the next year.

decisions.choice: locusts: swarms of locusts
decisions.reason: Gobay is a word for locusts (Nahum 3:17). A swarm could strip a land bare (Joel 1:4). The LORD is 'forming' them, the word used of a potter shaping clay: the plague is his work.

decisions.choice: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: look (L); This is what the Lord GOD showed me (B); The Lord GOD showed me a vision (R)
decisions.reason: The opening formula of the visions keeps one wording at each level in 7:1, 4, 7 and 8:1. 'Look' (hinneh) is kept at Literal and left to the sense at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: swarms of; the crop that grows after (B); the second crop; of the first crop (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain what the late crop and the king's mowings were (m2).

decisions.choice: "Así me mostró el Señor DIOS: he aquí" (L), "Esto es lo que me mostró el Señor DIOS" (B), "El Señor DIOS me mostró una visión" (R)
decisions.reason: One wording per level for the opening of the visions in 7:1, 4, 7 and 8:1.

decisions.choice: passé simple at L and B ("me fit voir", "je dis"), passé composé at R ("m'a montré", "j'ai dit")
decisions.reason: Amos's visions (7:1-9) and the story of Amaziah (7:10-17) are narrative, told by Amos in the first person; the words spoken inside them keep the tenses of speech.

decisions.choice: "Bwana MUNGU alinionyesha hivi: tazama" (L), "Hiki ndicho Bwana MUNGU alichonionyesha" (B), "alinionyesha maono" (R); "mmea wa pili" for the late crop
decisions.reason: One opening per level for the visions of 7:1, 4, 7 and 8:1, told with the narrative -li- and -ka-. Leqesh is the second growth after the spring rains, so "mmea wa pili".

decisions.choice: "Chúa là CHÚA cho tôi thấy thế này: kìa" (L), "Đây là điều Chúa là CHÚA cho tôi thấy" (B), "cho tôi thấy một khải tượng" (R)
decisions.reason: One opening per level for the visions of 7:1, 4, 7 and 8:1; Amos narrates as "tôi".

decisions.choice: "주 하나님께서 나에게 이와 같이 보여 주셨다" (L), "…보여 주신 것은 이러하다" (B), "…환상을 보여 주셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: One opening per level for the visions of 7:1, 4, 7 and 8:1. Amos narrates in the plain style with -시- for God.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־כִּלָּה֙ לֶֽאֱכוֹל֙ אֶת־עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֔רֶץ וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ סְֽלַֽח־נָ֔א מִ֥י יָק֖וּם יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י קָטֹ֖ן הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when it had finished eating the vegetation of the land, I said, Lord Yahweh, forgive, please! How will Jacob stand? For he [is] small.

en.L: And it happened, when they had finished eating the vegetation of the land, that I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, forgive, please! How can Jacob stand? For he [is] small."
en.B: When they had eaten up the green plants of the land, I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please forgive! How can Jacob survive? He is so small."
en.R: The locusts ate every green plant in the land. Then I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please forgive your people! How can Israel survive? It is so small and weak."

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando terminaron de comer la hierba de la tierra, dije: «Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, ¡perdona, por favor! ¿Cómo podrá mantenerse Jacob? Porque [es] pequeño».
es.B: Cuando acabaron con la vegetación del país, dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, perdona, por favor! ¿Cómo podrá sobrevivir Jacob? ¡Es tan pequeño!».
es.R: Las langostas se comieron todas las plantas verdes del país. Entonces dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, por favor, perdona a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo! ¿Cómo podrá sobrevivir Israel? ¡Es tan pequeño y débil!».

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand elles eurent fini de manger l’herbe du pays, que je dis : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, pardonne, de grâce ! Comment Jacob tiendra-t-il debout ? Car il [est] petit. »
fr.B: Quand elles eurent dévoré la verdure du pays, je dis : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, pardonne, de grâce ! Comment Jacob pourra-t-il survivre ? Il est si petit. »
fr.R: Les sauterelles ont mangé toutes les plantes vertes du pays. Alors j’ai dit : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, de grâce, pardonne à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple ! Comment Israël pourra-t-il survivre ? Il est si petit et si faible ! »

sw.L: Ikawa, walipokwisha kula mimea ya nchi, nikasema, "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, samehe, tafadhali! Yakobo atasimamaje? Kwa maana yeye [ni] mdogo."
sw.B: Walipokwisha kula mimea yote ya nchi, nikasema, "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali samehe! Yakobo ataweza kuishije? Yeye ni mdogo mno."
sw.R: Nzige walikula kila mmea wa kijani katika nchi. Kisha nikasema, "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali uwasamehe watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}! Israeli itaishije? Ni ndogo mno na dhaifu."

vi.L: Và xảy ra, khi chúng đã ăn hết cây cỏ trong xứ, thì tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tha thứ! Gia-cốp làm sao đứng nổi? Vì nó [thì] nhỏ bé."
vi.B: Khi chúng đã ăn sạch cây cỏ trong xứ, tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tha thứ! Gia-cốp làm sao sống sót nổi? Nó nhỏ bé quá."
vi.R: Châu chấu ăn sạch mọi cây xanh trong xứ. Bấy giờ tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tha thứ cho dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}! Y-sơ-ra-ên làm sao sống sót nổi? Dân ấy nhỏ bé và yếu đuối quá."

ko.L: 그것들이 그 땅의 풀을 다 먹어 치웠을 때에 내가 말씀드렸다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 부디 용서하여 주십시오! 야곱이 어떻게 서겠습니까? 그는 작습니다."
ko.B: 메뚜기들이 그 땅의 푸성귀를 다 먹어 버렸을 때에 내가 말씀드렸다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 제발 용서하여 주십시오! 야곱이 어떻게 살아남겠습니까? 그는 너무나 작습니다."
ko.R: 메뚜기들이 그 땅의 푸른 풀을 모두 먹어 버렸다. 그때에 내가 말씀드렸다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 제발 주님의 백성을 용서하여 주십시오! 이스라엘이 어떻게 살아남겠습니까? 이스라엘은 너무 작고 약합니다."

decisions.choice: when they had finished eating: Amos prays as the locusts finish their work
alternatives: if they finished eating (a warning before it happens)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew 'and it was, if they finished' is unusual. It is usually read as 'when they had finished'. In the vision Amos sees the crop all but gone, and he prays before the picture becomes fact.

decisions.choice: forgive: pardon the people's sin, and so hold back the judgment
decisions.reason: Amos does not deny that the people deserve judgment; he asks the LORD to pardon them. In the second vision he asks only that the LORD stop (verse 5).

decisions.choice: How can Jacob stand? He is small: Israel is too weak to survive such a blow
decisions.reason: Amos calls the people 'Jacob', the name of their ancestor, and pleads that they are small and helpless. The rich of Samaria thought themselves 'the first of the nations' (6:1); the prophet sees how small they are before the LORD.

decisions.choice: survive (B, R); Israel; your people; small and weak (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'survive' for 'stand'. Readable says 'Israel' for 'Jacob', adds 'your people' as the object of 'forgive', and adds 'weak' to bring out what 'small' means here (m3).

decisions.choice: "de grâce" for the particle na'
decisions.reason: The plea keeps the urgency of na' without a pronoun for God that would need a setting span; 7:5 has the same wording.

decisions.choice: 합쇼체 for Amos's prayer, with the bare vocative "주 하나님,"
decisions.reason: A prophet speaks to God in 합쇼체; after the divine-name span no vocative particle is added, so that both forms of the setting read correctly.

source.text: נִחַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־זֹ֑את לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh relented concerning this. It will not be, said Yahweh.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning this. "It will not happen," said {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented. "It will not happen," {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind. "It will not happen," said {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se retractó de esto. «No sucederá», dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} desistió. «No sucederá», dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} cambió de parecer. «Eso no sucederá», dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} renonça à cela. « Cela n’arrivera pas », dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} y renonça. « Cela n’arrivera pas », dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a changé d’avis. « Cela n’arrivera pas », a dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akabadili nia {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Jambo hilo halitatokea."

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý về điều này. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều ấy sẽ không xảy ra."
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều ấy sẽ không xảy ra."
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều đó sẽ không xảy ra đâu."

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 일에 대하여 뜻을 돌이키셨다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 "그 일이 일어나지 않을 것이다" 하고 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 뜻을 돌이키셨다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "그 일이 일어나지 않을 것이다."
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 마음을 바꾸셨다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "그 일은 일어나지 않을 것이다."

decisions.choice: relented: the LORD turned back from the judgment he had shown
decisions.reason: Nicham means to be sorry or to change one's course. It is often used of the LORD holding back a punishment he had announced (Exodus 32:14; Jeremiah 18:8; Jonah 3:10). It shows that the prophet's prayer mattered. It does not mean that the LORD had done wrong.

decisions.choice: changed his mind (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says 'changed his mind' for 'relented', in the sense explained in m1.

decisions.choice: "se retractó" (L), "desistió" (B), "cambió de parecer" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the LORD relenting in Exodus 32:14 and Jonah 3:10; "arrepentirse" would suggest that he had done wrong (m1). 7:6 repeats it.

decisions.choice: "akaghairi" (L, B), "akabadili nia yake" (R)
decisions.reason: As Exodus 32:14 and Jonah 3:10; 7:6 repeats it.

decisions.choice: "뜻을 돌이키셨다" (L, B), "마음을 바꾸셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: As Exodus 32:14 and Jonah 3:10; the LORD turns back from the judgment without having done wrong (m1).

source.text: כֹּ֤ה הִרְאַ֨נִי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה קֹרֵ֛א לָרִ֥ב בָּאֵ֖שׁ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ אֶת־תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וְאָכְלָ֖ה אֶת־הַחֵֽלֶק׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus showed me [the] Lord Yahweh, and look, [the] Lord Yahweh [was] calling to contend by fire; and it devoured the great deep, and it was devouring the portion.

en.L: Thus the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: look, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} was calling to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep and was devouring the portion [of land].
en.B: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: there was the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, summoning fire to judge. It dried up the great deep and was eating up the land.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me another vision. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} was calling for fire to punish the people. The fire dried up the deep waters under the earth and began to burn up the land.

es.L: Así me mostró el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: he aquí, el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} llamaba a juicio por fuego, y este devoró el gran abismo y devoraba la porción [de tierra].
es.B: Esto es lo que me mostró el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: allí estaba el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, convocando el fuego para juzgar. El fuego secó el gran abismo y estaba devorando la tierra.
es.R: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} me mostró otra visión. El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} estaba llamando al fuego para castigar al pueblo. El fuego secó las aguas profundas que hay debajo de la tierra y comenzó a quemar los campos.

fr.L: Ainsi me fit voir le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : voici, le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} appelait à plaider par le feu, et il dévora le grand abîme et il dévorait la part [de terre].
fr.B: Voici ce que le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} me fit voir : le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} appelait le feu pour juger. Le feu assécha le grand abîme et il dévorait le pays.
fr.R: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} m’a montré une autre vision. Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} appelait le feu pour punir le peuple. Le feu a asséché les eaux profondes qui sont sous la terre, et il a commencé à brûler le pays.

sw.L: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alinionyesha hivi: tazama, Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alikuwa akiita kushindana kwa moto, nao ukakila kilindi kikuu, na ulikuwa ukilila fungu [la nchi].
sw.B: Hiki ndicho Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alichonionyesha: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alikuwa akiuita moto ili kuhukumu. Moto ukakausha kilindi kikuu, na ulikuwa ukiila nchi.
sw.R: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alinionyesha maono mengine. Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alikuwa akiuita moto ili kuwaadhibu watu. Moto ukakausha maji ya vilindi vilivyo chini ya ardhi, ukaanza kuiteketeza nchi.

vi.L: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy thế này: kìa, Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang gọi để tranh tụng bằng lửa, và lửa thiêu nuốt vực sâu lớn và đang thiêu nuốt phần [đất].
vi.B: Đây là điều Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang gọi lửa đến để xét xử. Lửa làm khô cạn vực sâu lớn và đang thiêu nuốt đất đai.
vi.R: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy một khải tượng khác. Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang gọi lửa đến để trừng phạt dân chúng. Lửa làm khô cạn những vùng nước sâu dưới lòng đất và bắt đầu thiêu đốt đất đai.

ko.L: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 이와 같이 보여 주셨다. 보라, 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 불로 심판하려고 부르고 계셨다. 그 불이 큰 깊음을 삼키고, 그 몫의 [땅]을 삼키고 있었다.
ko.B: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 보여 주신 것은 이러하다. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 심판하시려고 불을 부르고 계셨다. 그 불이 큰 깊음을 말려 버리고 땅을 삼키고 있었다.
ko.R: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 또 다른 환상을 보여 주셨다. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 백성을 벌하시려고 불을 부르고 계셨다. 그 불이 땅 밑의 깊은 물을 말려 버리고 땅을 태우기 시작했다.

decisions.choice: calling to contend by fire: summoning fire to carry out his case against Israel
alternatives: calling for a rain of fire (dividing the letters as lirvivei 'esh)
decisions.reason: Riv is a legal case, and the LORD calls for fire to carry out his judgment (compare Isaiah 66:16). The phrase 'to contend by fire' is unusual, and some divide the letters differently to read 'calling for a shower of fire'. The sense is close either way: a fire of judgment sent by the LORD.

decisions.choice: the great deep: the waters under the earth that feed springs and rivers
decisions.reason: Tehom rabbah is the great deep, the waters below the earth (Genesis 7:11; Isaiah 51:10). This fire is so fierce that it dries up the sources of water, and then it begins on the land.

decisions.choice: the portion: the land given to Israel as its share
decisions.reason: Cheleq is a share or allotted portion, here the farmland divided among Israel's families (Micah 2:4). The fire is eating up the land itself.

decisions.choice: summoning fire to judge (B); to punish the people (R); dried up; the land (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'the land' for 'the portion' (m3) and 'dried up' for what fire does to water. Readable explains 'the great deep' (m2) and says what the fire is for.

records.literal_gloss: And I said, Lord Yahweh, cease, please! How will Jacob stand? For he [is] small.

en.R: Then I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please stop! How can Israel survive? It is so small and weak."

es.R: Entonces dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, detente, por favor! ¿Cómo podrá sobrevivir Israel? ¡Es tan pequeño y débil!».

sw.B: Ndipo nikasema, "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali acha! Yakobo ataweza kuishije? Yeye ni mdogo mno."
sw.R: Ndipo nikasema, "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali acha! Israeli itaishije? Ni ndogo mno na dhaifu."

decisions.choice: cease: Amos now asks only that the LORD hold back
decisions.reason: In verse 2 Amos asked the LORD to forgive; now he asks only that he stop. The rest of the plea repeats verse 2 word for word, and the wording here repeats it at each level.

decisions.choice: 'anakh: a plumb line, a weight of lead or tin hung on a cord
alternatives: tin: a wall of tin, and tin in his hand
decisions.reason: The word 'anakh is found only in verses 7-8. It has long been understood as a plumb line, a weight hung on a cord to test whether a wall is straight. In Akkadian, a related language, the word means tin, and some take the vision to show the Lord holding tin: perhaps a picture of weapons, or of a wall that cannot stand, or a play on a word for groaning. The plumb line fits verse 8 best: the LORD will test his people as a builder tests a wall, and a crooked wall comes down (compare 2 Kings 21:13; Isaiah 28:17).

decisions.choice: the Lord was standing: Amos sees the Lord himself in this vision
decisions.reason: In the first two visions Amos was shown what the Lord was doing; here he sees the Lord himself, standing beside the wall. The usual words 'the Lord GOD' are shortened to 'he' and 'the Lord'.

decisions.choice: built true to a plumb line (B); built straight (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what 'a wall of a plumb line' means: a wall built straight, checked with a plumb line (m1). Readable names the Lord at the start, since 'he' alone would be unclear.

decisions.choice: "plomada"; "un muro hecho a plomada" (L, B), "un muro construido bien derecho" (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 21:13 and the English plumb line; the reading "tin" is given in the English note (m1).

decisions.choice: "un fil à plomb" at every level
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 21:13 B; the reading "tin" stays in the English note (m1).

decisions.choice: "timazi" at every level
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 21:13 and Isaiah 28:17; the reading "tin" stays in the English note (m1).

decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 21:13; the reading "tin" stays in the English note (m1).

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh said to me, What [are] you seeing, Amos? And I said, A plumb line. And [the] Lord said, Look, I [am] setting a plumb line in [the] midst of my people Israel; I will not again pass by him anymore.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A plumb line." And the Lord said, "Look, I am putting a plumb line in the midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel; never again will I pass by them.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "What do you see, Amos?" I answered, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Look, I am placing a plumb line among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. I will no longer pass them by.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "Amos, what do you see?" I answered, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "I am going to test {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel with a plumb line, to see whether they are straight. I will not let them go unpunished any longer.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «¿Qué ves, Amós?». Y dije: «Una plomada». Y el Señor dijo: «He aquí, yo pongo una plomada en medio de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel; nunca más volveré a pasar de largo ante él.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me preguntó: «¿Qué ves, Amós?». Respondí: «Una plomada». Entonces el Señor dijo: «Mira, voy a poner una plomada en medio de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel. Ya no volveré a pasarlos por alto.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me preguntó: «Amós, ¿qué ves?». Respondí: «Una plomada». Entonces el Señor dijo: «Voy a probar a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel con una plomada, para ver si está derecho. Ya no dejaré que siga sin castigo.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Que vois-tu, Amos ? » Et je dis : « Un fil à plomb. » Et le Seigneur dit : « Voici, je mets un fil à plomb au milieu de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël ; plus jamais je ne passerai outre.

decisions.choice: setting a plumb line in the midst of my people: testing Israel and finding it crooked
decisions.reason: A builder holds a plumb line against a wall to see whether it is straight, and a wall that leans has to be pulled down. The LORD is testing his people by his standard, and verse 9 gives the result.

decisions.choice: I will not pass by them again: I will no longer spare them
decisions.reason: To pass by someone is to overlook their wrong and spare them (Micah 7:18; Proverbs 19:11). In the first two visions the LORD relented; now he says he will not spare them again. 8:2 repeats the line. Compare 5:17, where he will pass through their midst to judge them.

decisions.choice: test ... to see whether they are straight; let them go unpunished (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what setting a plumb line among the people means (m1) and what 'pass by' means (m2).

decisions.choice: "plus jamais je ne passerai outre" (L), "Je ne fermerai plus les yeux sur ses fautes" (B), "Je ne le laisserai plus sans punition" (R)
alternatives: "je ne passerai plus à côté de lui"
decisions.reason: To pass by someone is to spare him (m2); "passer outre" keeps the verb "passer" with the sense of overlooking. 8:2 repeats the wording.

decisions.choice: God to Amos: "ngươi" (L), "con" (B, R); Amos: "tôi thưa"
decisions.reason: The address settled for God speaking to the prophets in these books; 8:2 follows it.

decisions.choice: God speaks 해라체 ("아모스야, … 보느냐?"); Amos answers 합쇼체 ("다림줄입니다")
decisions.reason: The speech levels settled for God and the prophets; 8:2 follows them.

decisions.choice: the high places of Isaac: hilltop shrines, named after Israel's ancestor Isaac
decisions.reason: Bamot were open-air shrines, often on hills. Only Amos calls Israel 'Isaac' (also verse 16). The name may point to Beersheba, which was linked with Isaac (5:5; 8:14; Genesis 26:23-25), or simply to the people as Isaac's descendants.

decisions.choice: the house of Jeroboam: the royal family of Jeroboam II
decisions.reason: Jeroboam II was king of Israel when Amos prophesied (1:1). His son Zechariah reigned only six months before he was murdered, and with him the family's rule ended (2 Kings 15:8-10).

decisions.choice: hilltop places where Isaac's people worship; King Jeroboam's family (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the high places were and who 'Isaac' is (m1), and that the house of Jeroboam is the king's family (m2).

ko.L: 그러자 벧엘의 제사장 아마샤가 이스라엘 왕 여로보암에게 [사람을] 보내어 말했다. "아모스가 이스라엘 집 한가운데서 임금님을 거슬러 반역을 꾀하였습니다. 이 땅이 그의 모든 말을 견딜 수 없습니다.

ko.R: 벧엘의 제사장 아마샤가 이스라엘 왕 여로보암에게 전갈을 보냈다. 그는 이렇게 말했다. "아모스가 바로 여기 이스라엘 백성 가운데서 임금님을 해치려고 음모를 꾸미고 있습니다. 이 나라는 그가 하는 말을 더 이상 참을 수 없습니다.

decisions.choice: a story set among the visions
decisions.reason: Verses 10-17 tell, in prose, how the priest of Bethel tried to silence Amos. The story follows the third vision because that vision ends with the sword against the house of Jeroboam (verse 9), the words Amaziah reports to the king (verse 11). It is the only story about Amos in the book, and it speaks of him in the third person.

decisions.choice: Amaziah the priest of Bethel: the chief priest of the royal shrine
decisions.reason: Bethel was the king's sanctuary (verse 13), set up by Jeroboam I (1 Kings 12:28-33). Amaziah is known only from this passage.

decisions.choice: conspired: plotted rebellion; the land cannot bear his words
decisions.reason: Qashar is the word for a political plot against a king (2 Kings 15:10). Amaziah presents Amos's words as treason. The land 'cannot bear' them, as a vessel cannot hold more than it can contain.

decisions.choice: passé simple at L and B ("envoya"), passé composé at R ("a envoyé"); Amatsia says "tu" to the king
decisions.reason: The story of 7:10-17 is narrative, told in the third person; one person addressed is "tu", the king included, as in Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: Amaziah to the king: "vua" (L), "bệ hạ" (B), "đức vua" (R); Amos is "ông ta"
decisions.reason: A subject speaking to the king uses the forms settled for the court; Amaziah's hostility to Amos is carried by his words, not by a coarse pronoun.

decisions.choice: 합쇼체 with "임금님" in Amaziah's message to the king
decisions.reason: The speech level settled for subjects speaking to a king.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam will die by the sword: Amaziah sharpens verse 9
decisions.reason: Amos had said that the LORD would rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword (verse 9), not that Jeroboam himself would die by it. decisions.choice: I am not a prophet, nor a prophet's son: Amos denies being a professional prophet
alternatives: I was not a prophet, nor a prophet's son (until the LORD called me)
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses no verb here, so the sentence can be read in the present ('I am not') or the past ('I was not'). In the present, Amos refuses Amaziah's picture of him as a prophet who earns his bread by prophesying (verse 12): he is not one of the professionals. In the past, he means that he was not a prophet until the LORD took him from the flock (verse 15). Either way, he prophesies because the LORD sent him, not because it is his trade; in verse 15 the LORD himself tells him to 'prophesy'.

decisions.choice: a son of a prophet: a member of a company of prophets
decisions.reason: 'Sons of the prophets' were groups of prophets who lived and worked together, often under a leader such as Elisha (2 Kings 2:3; 4:38). 'Son' here means a member or disciple, not a child. Amos says that he never belonged to such a group.

decisions.choice: a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs
decisions.reason: Boqer is one who keeps cattle (baqar). In 1:1 Amos is called one of the sheep breeders of Tekoa, and in verse 15 the LORD took him 'from following the flock'. The sycamore fig is a kind of fig tree that grew in the warm lowlands (1 Kings 10:27). Its fruit had to be slit or pinched while growing so that it would ripen and be sweet, and boles seems to name that work. Amos may have owned flocks and orchards or worked for others; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: a member of a company of prophets (B); trained as a prophet; raise livestock; fig trees (R)
decisions.reason: Ben-navi' is 'a son of a prophet' at Literal, 'a member of a company of prophets' at Balanced and 'trained as a prophet' at Readable, as 2 Kings 2:3 and the terms note settle (m2). Readable says 'I was not trained' for the present 'I am not a son of a prophet', which comes to the same thing. It says 'raise livestock' for 'herdsman' and 'fig trees' for 'sycamore figs'.

decisions.reason: Even when he sends Amos with words of judgment, the LORD calls Israel 'my people' (7:8; 8:2).

decisions.choice: passé composé at every level ("m'a pris", "m'a dit")
decisions.reason: Amos is speaking to Amatsia, so his account of his call keeps the tenses of speech, not the passé simple of the narrative around it.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֗ר לֹ֤א תִנָּבֵא֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א תַטִּ֖יף עַל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂחָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And now hear the word of Yahweh. You [are] saying, You shall not prophesy against Israel, and you shall not drip against the house of Isaac.

en.L: And now hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You are saying, 'You shall not prophesy against Israel, and you shall not drip [words] against the house of Isaac.'
en.B: So now hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You tell me, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and stop preaching against the house of Isaac.'
en.R: Now listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. You tell me, 'Do not prophesy against Israel. Stop preaching against the people of Isaac.'

es.L: Y ahora oye la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Tú dices: “No profetizarás contra Israel, ni destilarás [palabras] contra la casa de Isaac”.
es.B: Así que ahora escucha la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Tú me dices: “No profetices contra Israel, y deja de predicar contra la casa de Isaac”.
es.R: Ahora escucha lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Tú me dices: “No profetices contra Israel. Deja de predicar contra el pueblo de Isaac”.

fr.L: Et maintenant écoute la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Tu dis : “Tu ne prophétiseras pas contre Israël, et tu ne laisseras pas couler [tes paroles] contre la maison d’Isaac.”
fr.B: Maintenant donc, écoute la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Tu me dis : “Ne prophétise pas contre Israël, et cesse de prêcher contre la maison d’Isaac.”
fr.R: Maintenant, écoute le message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Tu me dis : “Ne prophétise pas contre Israël. Arrête de prêcher contre le peuple d’Isaac.”

sw.L: Basi sasa sikia neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wewe unasema, 'Usitoe unabii juu ya Israeli, wala usidondoshe [maneno] juu ya nyumba ya Isaka.'
sw.B: Basi sasa sikiliza neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wewe unaniambia, 'Usitoe unabii dhidi ya Israeli, na uache kuhubiri dhidi ya nyumba ya Isaka.'
sw.R: Sasa sikiliza ujumbe huu kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wewe unaniambia, 'Usitoe unabii dhidi ya Israeli. Acha kuhubiri dhidi ya wazao wa Isaka.'

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, hãy nghe lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ông nói: 'Chớ nói tiên tri nghịch cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên, và chớ nhỏ [lời] nghịch cùng nhà Y-sác.'
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, hãy nghe lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ông bảo tôi: 'Đừng nói tiên tri nghịch cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên, và thôi rao giảng nghịch cùng nhà Y-sác.'
vi.R: Bây giờ, hãy nghe điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Ông bảo tôi: 'Đừng nói tiên tri nghịch cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên. Thôi đừng rao giảng nghịch cùng dòng dõi Y-sác nữa.'

ko.L: 그러니 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀을 들어라. 너는 '이스라엘을 거슬러 예언하지 말고, 이삭의 집을 거슬러 [말을] 떨어뜨리지 마라' 하고 말한다.
ko.B: 그러니 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀을 들어라. 너는 나에게 '이스라엘을 거슬러 예언하지 말고, 이삭의 집을 거슬러 설교하지 마라' 하고 말한다.
ko.R: 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀을 들어라. 너는 나에게 '이스라엘을 거슬러 예언하지 마라. 이삭의 자손을 거슬러 설교하지 마라' 하고 말한다.

decisions.choice: drip words: preach, let words fall like drops
decisions.reason: Hittif, 'to drip', is used of speaking or preaching (Micah 2:6, 11; Ezekiel 21:2). It may carry a note of scorn, like 'drivel'.

decisions.choice: you say: Amos quotes Amaziah's order back to him
decisions.reason: Amaziah's words of verse 13 are given again in a sharper form, now as the very thing for which judgment will come. Israel and the house of Isaac are the same people (verse 9).

decisions.choice: preaching (B, R); the people of Isaac (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1). Readable says 'people' for 'house'.

decisions.choice: "destilarás [palabras]" (L), "predicar" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of words falling like drops; Balanced and Readable give its sense (m1).

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֞ בָּעִ֤יר תִּזְנֶה֙ וּבָנֶ֤יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ וְאַדְמָתְךָ֖ בַּחֶ֣בֶל תְּחֻלָּ֑ק וְאַתָּ֗ה עַל־אֲדָמָ֤ה טְמֵאָה֙ תָּמ֔וּת וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל גָּלֹ֥ה יִגְלֶ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: Your wife in the city will be a prostitute, and your sons and your daughters by the sword will fall, and your land by a measuring line will be divided, and you on unclean ground will die, and Israel will surely go into exile from upon its land.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Your wife in the city will be a prostitute, and your sons and your daughters by the sword will fall, and your land will be divided up by measuring line; and you yourself will die on unclean ground, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'Your wife will be made a prostitute in the city, your sons and daughters will be struck down by the sword, and your land will be measured out and divided. You yourself will die in an unclean land, and Israel will surely go into exile, away from its land.'"
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'Your wife will have to become a prostitute in the city. Your sons and daughters will be killed by the sword. Your land will be measured and divided up among others. You yourself will die in a foreign land, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is not worshiped. And the people of Israel will surely be taken from their land as captives.'"

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “Tu mujer se prostituirá en la ciudad, y tus hijos y tus hijas caerán a espada, y tu tierra será repartida a cordel; y tú mismo morirás en tierra inmunda, e Israel ciertamente irá al destierro lejos de su tierra”».
es.B: Por eso, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: “Tu mujer será prostituida en la ciudad, tus hijos y tus hijas caerán a espada, y tu tierra será medida y repartida. Tú mismo morirás en una tierra impura, e Israel será desterrado sin falta, lejos de su tierra”».
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “Tu esposa tendrá que hacerse prostituta en la ciudad. Tus hijos y tus hijas morirán a espada. Tu tierra será medida y repartida entre otros. Tú mismo morirás en una tierra extranjera, donde no se adora {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Y el pueblo de Israel será llevado prisionero lejos de su tierra, sin duda alguna”».

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : “Ta femme se prostituera dans la ville, et tes fils et tes filles tomberont par l’épée, et ta terre sera partagée au cordeau ; et toi, tu mourras sur une terre impure, et Israël ira certainement en exil loin de sa terre.” »
fr.B: C’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : “Ta femme sera prostituée dans la ville, tes fils et tes filles tomberont par l’épée, et ta terre sera mesurée et partagée. Toi-même, tu mourras sur une terre impure, et Israël sera certainement exilé loin de sa terre.” »
fr.R: C’est pourquoi voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : “Ta femme devra se prostituer dans la ville. Tes fils et tes filles seront tués par l’épée. Ta terre sera mesurée et partagée entre d’autres. Toi-même, tu mourras dans un pays étranger, où l’on n’adore pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et le peuple d’Israël sera sûrement emmené en captivité loin de son pays.” »

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: 'Mke wako atakuwa kahaba mjini, na wana wako na binti zako wataanguka kwa upanga, na nchi yako itagawanywa kwa kamba ya kupimia; nawe mwenyewe utakufa katika nchi iliyo najisi, na Israeli hakika atachukuliwa uhamishoni kutoka katika nchi yake.'"
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: 'Mke wako atafanywa kahaba mjini, wana wako na binti zako watauawa kwa upanga, na nchi yako itapimwa na kugawanywa. Wewe mwenyewe utafia katika nchi najisi, na Israeli hakika atapelekwa uhamishoni, mbali na nchi yake.'"
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: 'Mke wako atalazimika kuwa kahaba mjini. Wana wako na binti zako watauawa kwa upanga. Nchi yako itapimwa na kugawanywa kwa watu wengine. Wewe mwenyewe utafia katika nchi ya kigeni, ambako {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} haabudiwi. Na watu wa Israeli hakika watachukuliwa mateka kutoka katika nchi yao.'"

vi.L: Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: 'Vợ ông sẽ làm gái mại dâm trong thành, các con trai và con gái ông sẽ ngã dưới gươm, đất của ông sẽ bị chia bằng dây đo; còn chính ông sẽ chết trên đất ô uế, và Y-sơ-ra-ên chắc chắn sẽ bị lưu đày khỏi xứ của mình.'"
vi.B: Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: 'Vợ ông sẽ bị bắt làm gái mại dâm trong thành, các con trai và con gái ông sẽ ngã chết dưới gươm, và đất của ông sẽ bị đo đạc và chia cắt. Chính ông sẽ chết nơi đất ô uế, và Y-sơ-ra-ên chắc chắn sẽ bị lưu đày xa khỏi quê hương mình.'"
vi.R: Vì vậy, đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: 'Vợ ông sẽ phải làm gái mại dâm trong thành. Các con trai và con gái ông sẽ bị giết bằng gươm. Đất của ông sẽ bị đo đạc và chia cho người khác. Chính ông sẽ chết nơi đất ngoại bang, là nơi người ta không thờ phượng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Và dân Y-sơ-ra-ên chắc chắn sẽ bị bắt đi làm phu tù khỏi xứ của mình.'"

ko.L: 그러므로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. '네 아내는 성읍에서 창녀가 되고, 네 아들들과 딸들은 칼에 쓰러지고, 네 땅은 측량줄로 나뉠 것이다. 너 자신은 부정한 땅에서 죽을 것이고, 이스라엘은 반드시 사로잡혀 자기 땅을 떠날 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그러므로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. '네 아내는 성읍에서 창녀가 되고, 네 아들들과 딸들은 칼에 맞아 쓰러지고, 네 땅은 측량되어 나뉠 것이다. 너 자신은 부정한 땅에서 죽을 것이고, 이스라엘은 반드시 사로잡혀 자기 땅에서 끌려갈 것이다.'"
ko.R: 그러므로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. '네 아내는 성읍에서 몸을 팔게 될 것이다. 네 아들들과 딸들은 칼에 죽을 것이다. 네 땅은 측량되어 다른 사람들에게 나뉠 것이다. 너 자신은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기지 않는 이방 땅에서 죽을 것이다. 그리고 이스라엘 백성은 틀림없이 포로가 되어 자기 땅에서 끌려갈 것이다.'"

decisions.choice: the fate of a conquered city
decisions.reason: Each line names what happened when a city fell: women were taken by the soldiers or left to support themselves by prostitution, the young were killed, and the land was measured out for new owners (Micah 2:4-5). Amaziah himself would die in exile.

decisions.choice: unclean ground: a foreign land
decisions.reason: Israel's land belonged to the LORD. Any other land was unclean, because other gods were worshiped there and its food was not dedicated to the LORD (Hosea 9:3-4; Ezekiel 4:13). A priest, whose life was bound up with what is clean and unclean, would die in such a place.

decisions.choice: Israel will surely go into exile: Amos repeats the words Amaziah reported
decisions.reason: Amos does not take back the words Amaziah complained of (verse 11); he repeats them word for word, as the LORD's sentence.

decisions.choice: be a prostitute (L); be made a prostitute (B); have to become a prostitute (R)
decisions.reason: Here zanah is used of real prostitution, not of Israel's unfaithfulness to God, so the wording settled for Hosea ('prostitute oneself', 'be unfaithful') is not used. Balanced says 'be made' and Readable 'have to', since in a conquered city it would be forced on her (m1).

decisions.choice: among others; a foreign land, where the LORD is not worshiped (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who will get the land (m1) and what 'unclean ground' means (m2).

decisions.choice: the last clause repeats 7:11 word for word at each level
decisions.reason: Amos gives back Amaziah's report as the LORD's sentence (m3), so the wording is kept the same.

decisions.choice: the last clause repeats 7:11 word for word at each level
decisions.reason: Amos gives back Amaziah's report as the LORD's sentence (m3).

decisions.choice: "atakuwa kahaba" (L), "atafanywa kahaba" (B), "atalazimika kuwa kahaba" (R); the last clause repeats 7:11 at each level
decisions.reason: Literal prostitution is said plainly with "kahaba", kept apart from "kufanya ukahaba" for Israel's unfaithfulness (terms note).

decisions.choice: "làm gái mại dâm" at every level; the last clause repeats 7:11
decisions.reason: Literal prostitution takes "làm gái mại dâm", as settled; "làm điếm" stays for Israel's unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: "창녀가 되고" (L, B), "몸을 팔게 될 것이다" (R); the last clause repeats 7:11
decisions.reason: Literal prostitution is said plainly; "음행하다" stays for Israel's unfaithfulness.
